38ecd939c5f91eb8.text: About 35,000 patients have waited more than a year, and without action that would be about 39,000 by the end of 2028. Plan B, with 5% more permanent capacity, a check of who still needs care and the longest waiters seen first, will bring that down to about 16,000. It costs about EUR 19.4 million of the EUR 20 million budget, and the whole list would fall from about 70,000 to about 57,000. A one-year initiative of the same cost gives about 4% fewer patient-months of long waiting, but more long waiters by 2028. In all six futures we tested, Plan B ended 2028 with fewer long waiters than the initiative. In the worst, about 31,000 would still wait over a year, and if a permanent treatment cost EUR 1,250 rather than EUR 1,100, the plan would go over budget.
38ecd939c5f91eb8.how: written for the book with claude-opus-5-5 (no live API call)

0947672828ca5da1.text: A one-year initiative works like [B4 Buying activity]: when the list is long we buy extra treatments, and long waits fall quickly. But the money comes out of the same budget as our own staff, so the gain is paid back later through [R3 Borrowing from next year], a reinforcing loop. Where the extra work is done as overtime, [R2 Burnout] wears down the people who must carry on afterwards. When the initiative stops, referrals again outrun treatments and the list climbs back. Plan B changes the rate itself: permanent capacity works every month, so it does not depend on [B3 Working harder] being kept up. Checking who still needs care is a one-off cut, and it must stay a check, not slide into [B2 Giving up], where patients drop off the list unseen. Seeing the longest waiters first changes who waits, not how many. One caution: as waits fall, [B1 Discouraged referrals], a balancing loop, weakens and some hidden demand comes back. So the list is likely to fall less than the model shows.
0947672828ca5da1.how: written for the book with claude-opus-5-5 (no live API call)

21cc6de64e1d6a8d.text: Good news for patients: Plan B will cut the hospital group's waiting list to 45,000 by 2028 and slash the number waiting over a year by more than half, guaranteed. Every future we modelled shows it working, and it comes in under the EUR 20 million budget.
